explanation:
The claim is real about the list screen, but narrower than "a trainer cannot read what a student sent".

CONFIRMED: D:\spot\src\app\trainer\chat.tsx:22 reads `useDb((s) => s.threads)` — the pre-schema42 AsyncStorage map — and builds every row's preview and timestamp from it (`const msgs = threads[s.profileId] ?? []`, lines 27-31). It never calls `getMyThreads()`, `findThread()` or `getMessages()` from D:\spot\src\lib\chat.ts. It has no import from '@/lib/chat' at all.

That map is now dead for chat text. The only writer of message rows into `useDb.threads` is the local `sendMessage` action at D:\spot\src\store\db.ts:538-544, and a repo-wide grep shows it has ZERO callers — `src/app/chat/[id].tsx:145` calls the server `sendMessage` from `@/lib/chat` instead, and that screen writes nothing back into `useDb.threads` (it only reads `s.threads[id]` at line 42 to render legacy workout-invite cards, line 161). The only remaining writers of that map are `proposeWorkout` (a partner-match invite, db.ts:523) and `acceptMatch` (which stores an empty array, db.ts:532). So for a student's `profileId`, `threads[s.profileId]` is `undefined` in every realistic case.

Consequence: every student row renders `last: null, at: null`, i.e. the literal string "Hələ mesaj yoxdur — ilk mesajı yaz" (line 75) no matter how many real messages that student sent, no timestamp is shown, there is no unread count, and the `.sort()` on line 31 compares '' to '' so activity ordering is inert. The user-side inbox does this correctly — D:\spot\src\app\chat\index.tsx:126 merges `getMyThreads()` server threads — the trainer panel was simply never updated.

NARROWER THAN CLAIMED: tapping a row navigates to `/chat/[id]` with `r.id = s.profileId` (chat.tsx:60), and `profileId` is `trainer_requests.from_profile` (D:\spot\src\lib\roles.ts:143), which is exactly the `profiles.id` used in `chat_threads.a_profile/b_profile`. `src/app/chat/[id].tsx:82-97` then calls the real `findThread`/`getMessages`, plus realtime. So a trainer who taps a student DOES see the real messages. What is broken is discovery: nothing in the trainer panel ever indicates a message arrived. The trainer tab bar (D:\spot\src\app\trainer\_layout.tsx:31-36) has only Panel / Şagirdlər / Proqramlar / Söhbət — no notification centre entry point exists in trainer mode (grep for 'notification' across src/app/trainer/*.tsx returns nothing), so the `message` notification created by `tg_notify_message` (schema42) is unreachable there too. A trainer looking at Söhbət sees "Hələ mesaj yoxdur" on every row and has no reason to tap.

Server side is fine and applied: a live read confirmed `public.chat_threads` and `public.messages` exist and the trainer-link relationship path is what `open_thread` requires. The instance currently holds 0 threads / 0 messages / 0 accepted trainer links, so this is proven from code, not from live rows.

It is in fact stored server-side and delivered to the student. The claim is false in the one direction that matters — it understates where the data goes.

findings.title: "Hələ söhbət yoxdur" is shown for threads the screen never queried
findings.evidence: Rows are derived solely from `active` (chat.tsx:21,25), i.e. trainer_requests with status='accepted' (src/lib/roles.ts:116,160). The empty state at chat.tsx:46-51 fires on `rows.length === 0`, which only means "no accepted students", not "no threads". A chat_threads row survives independently of the request status — src/lib/roles.ts:21 already types 'ended' — and the trainer panel has no other inbox.
findings.failure: A trainer whose only student link later moves out of 'accepted' opens Söhbət and reads "Hələ söhbət yoxdur" while the conversation and its history still exist on the server. The archive becomes unreachable from trainer mode.
findings.fix: Drive the list from `getMyThreads()` and union it with the students list, so a thread with no matching active student still appears; reserve the empty state for a successful fetch that returned both zero threads and zero students.

explanation:
The RPC half of the claim is exactly right and reproducible; the "crashes" half is wrong — the panel degrades silently and fabricates zeros instead.

1) The live function body still sums the dropped column. Queried pg_proc on the linked project:

  'revenue_commission', (select coalesce(sum(commission),0) from public.day_passes where status in ('used','active'))

2) The column is really gone. information_schema.columns for public.day_passes returns exactly: id, user_id, gym_id, code, price, status, purchased_at, expires_at, refunded_at, refund_reason. No commission. pg_attribute reports attisdropped = 1 on that table, the tombstone of the dropped column.

3) It fails for every caller. `select public.admin_dashboard()` returns:
   ERROR: 42703: column "commission" does not exist
   CONTEXT: SQL function "admin_dashboard" during startup
   "during startup" matters: a LANGUAGE sql body is parse-analysed as a whole before the `case when public.is_admin(auth.uid())` branch is evaluated, so the non-admin `else '{}'::jsonb` path never saves it either. proacl grants EXECUTE to anon and authenticated, so any caller gets a 400 — but in practice only admins reach it.

4) Cause: D:\spot\supabase\schema27_trust_columns.sql:194 runs `alter table public.day_passes drop column if exists commission` (deliberately — the comment says a commission column "is a place for a number to appear later") but never redefines admin_dashboard. No later migration redefines it; grep over D:\spot\supabase shows admin_dashboard only in schema4_admin.sql and verify_schema.sql. The rest of the codebase was cleaned properly — src/lib/api.ts:806-808 and web/admin/src/lib/types.ts:143 both explain the removal, web/admin/src/screens/Analytics.tsx:115 has no revenue metric, and the DashboardKpis interface (types.ts:206-214) has no revenue_commission field. The live SQL function is the only thing left behind.

5) It does NOT crash. Both call sites destructure only `data` and discard `error`:
   - D:\spot\web\admin\src\App.tsx:35 — `const { data } = await supabase.rpc('admin_dashboard');` then `(data ?? {})`, so every sidebar badge collapses to '' and disappears.
   - D:\spot\web\admin\src\screens\Dashboard.tsx:36 — k stays null. The five KPI tiles correctly render '—' (that part is honest), but the three SLA queue cards at lines 78/80/82 use `count={k?.trainers_pending ?? 0}`, printing a hard 0.

6) Live proof of the resulting lie, from the same project right now: 1 pending trainer verification, 5 open reports, 0 pending claims. So today an admin's dashboard header reads "Şikayətlər 0" while 5 reports are open, and "Müəllim doğrulanması 0" while 1 is waiting — and QueueCard's `rows` come from separate working queries, so the SLA rows underneath list those very items next to the 0. The sidebar shows no badge at all.

Who is affected: every admin, on every load of the dashboard screen and every refreshCounts() call. Guests and normal app users are unaffected — the mobile client never calls this RPC.

Note for the fix: schema4_admin.sql:157 still declares `commission numeric(10,2)` in the base `create table`, so a fresh bootstrap that runs schema4 → schema27 ends in the correct state, but the function must be redefined without the `revenue_commission` key entirely rather than repointed at `price` — summing day-pass prices into a dashboard total is itself the revenue surface product rule 1 forbids, and the DashboardKpis type already has no field for it.

findings.title: admin_dashboard() RPC is dead — it sums the dropped day_passes.commission column and raises 42703 for every caller
findings.evidence: pg_proc.prosrc on the linked project still contains `'revenue_commission', (select coalesce(sum(commission),0) from public.day_passes where status in ('used','active'))`. information_schema.columns for public.day_passes lists only id, user_id, gym_id, code, price, status, purchased_at, expires_at, refunded_at, refund_reason — no commission — and pg_attribute shows attisdropped=1. Calling `select public.admin_dashboard()` returns `ERROR: 42703: column "commission" does not exist / CONTEXT: SQL function "admin_dashboard" during startup`. supabase/schema27_trust_columns.sql:194 dropped the column and no migration ever redefined the function.
findings.failure: Any admin loads the admin SPA. Both supabase.rpc('admin_dashboard') calls return a 400 with SQLSTATE 42703 instead of the KPI object. Because a LANGUAGE sql body is parse-analysed before the `case when public.is_admin(auth.uid())` branch runs, even a non-admin caller gets the error rather than the intended '{}' — the function has no working path at all.
findings.fix: Redefine public.admin_dashboard() in a new migration with the 'revenue_commission' key removed entirely (do not repoint it at day_passes.price — a revenue total is a product-rule-1 blocker, and web/admin/src/lib/types.ts:206-214 already models no such field). Also drop the stale `commission` column from the base create table at supabase/schema4_admin.sql:157 so a fresh bootstrap never recreates it.

findings.title: Failed dashboard RPC is rendered as a real 0 on the three SLA queue cards
findings.evidence: Line 36 discards the error (`const { data: kpi } = await supabase.rpc('admin_dashboard')`), leaving k null. Lines 78, 80 and 82 then pass `count={k?.trainers_pending ?? 0}`, `count={k?.reports_open ?? 0}` and `count={k?.claims_pending ?? 0}` into QueueCard, which prints the number unconditionally at line 115. The KPI tiles at lines 55-59 handle the same null honestly with '—', so the `?? 0` is the outlier.
findings.failure: Live counts on this project right now are 1 pending trainer verification and 5 open reports. Because the RPC 500s, an admin opening the dashboard today sees 'Şikayətlər 0' and 'Müəllim doğrulanması 0' — while the SLA rows rendered directly underneath (loaded by separate, working queries at lines 37-39) list those very open reports. A moderator reading the header count concludes the queue is clear and skips 5 open reports.
findings.fix: Track the RPC error and render '—' for the queue counts exactly as the KPI tiles do: capture `error` from the rpc call and pass `count={k ? k.reports_open : null}`, with QueueCard rendering '—' for null. Never coalesce a failed read to 0.

findings.title: Sidebar queue badges silently vanish because the dashboard RPC error is discarded
findings.evidence: `const { data } = await supabase.rpc('admin_dashboard');` drops the error, then `const k = (data ?? {}) as Partial<DashboardKpis>` makes every field undefined, so lines 38-41 set users/trainers/gyms/moderation to '' and the badges render empty. refreshCounts is also handed to every screen via props (line 68), so post-action refreshes fail the same way.
findings.failure: An admin signs in with 1 pending trainer verification and 5 open reports outstanding. The 'Müəllim' and 'Moderasiya' sidebar items show no badge at all, which is indistinguishable from an empty queue, so the pending work is never surfaced in navigation.
findings.fix: Destructure `error` too and render a distinct failure marker (e.g. '!') rather than '' when the call fails, so a broken read is visibly different from an empty queue.

explanation:
The claim is true in every particular. There is no push delivery of any kind — not a library, not a token, not an Edge Function, not even native credentials.

WHAT I CHECKED

1. No push library. D:\spot\package.json lists no `expo-notifications`, no OneSignal, no `@react-native-firebase/*`. A grep of node_modules for `notif|push|fcm|firebase|onesignal` returns exactly one directory, `safe-push-apply` (an unrelated array helper). A grep across all of D:\spot\src for `expo-notifications|getExpoPushToken|push_token|pushToken|scheduleNotificationAsync|setNotificationHandler|registerForPushNotifications|OneSignal|firebase` returns zero matches.

2. No native push config. D:\spot\app.json:42-68 lists plugins expo-router, expo-splash-screen, expo-font, expo-video, expo-audio — no expo-notifications. `find android -name google-services.json -o -name GoogleService-Info.plist` returns nothing. android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml contains no notification, firebase, gcm or POST_NOTIFICATIONS entry. D:\spot\eas.json has no push credential config.

3. No push token stored, verified against the live database:
   select table_name, column_name from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and (column_name ilike '%push%' or '%token%' or '%device%' or '%fcm%' or '%apns%' or '%expo%')
   → "rows": []. Not one column anywhere in the public schema.

4. No Edge Function. There is no D:\spot\supabase\functions directory at all; supabase/ holds only .sql files.

5. Notifications are rows and nothing else. D:\spot\supabase\schema35_notifications.sql creates public.notifications and a `notify()` SECURITY DEFINER function whose entire body is an INSERT. Live pg_trigger query confirms seven notify triggers (comment_likes, comments, follows, match_requests, messages, reviews, trainer_requests). Every one of them ends at the INSERT. Nothing calls pg_net, nothing posts to exp.host.

6. The only live delivery that exists is scoped to one already-open screen. D:\spot\src\lib\chat.ts:156 `subscribeToThread` opens a Supabase realtime channel `thread:${threadId}` filtered to that one thread. It only fires while the user is already looking at that exact conversation. There is no realtime subscription on the notifications table anywhere in the app.

7. Even in-app discovery is weak. D:\spot\src\app\(tabs)\discover\index.tsx:54-60 calls getUnreadCount() inside useFocusEffect — the unread badge refreshes only when the user navigates to the Discover tab. It is not on the tab bar, not polled, not pushed.

PRODUCT IMPACT — flows that silently depend on the user opening the app

match_request / match_accepted (partner matching, the app's core loop), message, trainer_request / trainer_decided, comment_reply, mention, follow, review_reply. All eight-plus real event types land in a table nobody is told about.

The worst case is messaging, and it is not merely slow — it deadlocks. D:\spot\supabase\schema42_real_messaging.sql:126-152 enforces "one message until reply": messages_gate() raises `wait_for_reply` (errcode 42501) if you already have one unanswered message in a thread. So person A sends a partner request, it is accepted, A sends one message — and is now hard-blocked from sending anything else until B replies. B is never told anything arrived. Neither side can nudge the other. The conversation is permanently stuck unless B independently reopens the app and taps into Discover. For a gym-partner app whose entire purpose is arranging to meet someone at a specific time, this makes the primary flow unreliable by construction.

WHAT WOULD BE NEEDED — and yes, it requires a native rebuild

Client: `expo-notifications` is a native module. Adding it cannot ship as an OTA update; every existing install needs a new binary. Concretely: add the dependency, add "expo-notifications" to app.json plugins, re-run prebuild over the committed android/ directory, then a fresh `expo run:android` / EAS build. Android also needs FCM V1 (a google-services.json plus a service-account key uploaded to EAS) and the Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission; iOS needs an APNs key and the aps-environment entitlement, which requires a paid Apple Developer account.

Server: a token table (profile_id, expo_push_token, platform, updated_at — with RLS so a token is writable only by its owner and readable by no client), plus an outbound call to https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send. The single correct hook point already exists: public.notify() in schema35 is where every notification row is born, so a pg_net call or a DB webhook fired from there covers all twelve types at once with no per-trigger changes.

Design note worth respecting: the notif_prefs check lives inside notify() before the INSERT, so a switched-off type is never recorded. Push must be gated at the same place, or a type the user turned off would still buzz their phone.

findings.title: No push notification delivery exists at all — notifications are database rows only
findings.evidence: public.notify() is a SECURITY DEFINER function whose entire body is `insert into public.notifications (...) values (...)` — it ends at the INSERT and calls nothing else. All seven live notify triggers (confirmed via pg_trigger: comment_likes, comments, follows, match_requests, messages, reviews, trainer_requests) route through it. There is no supabase/functions directory, so no Edge Function exists. A live information_schema.columns query for any column matching %push%/%token%/%device%/%fcm%/%apns%/%expo% in the public schema returned zero rows — no push token is stored anywhere. package.json contains no expo-notifications/OneSignal/firebase; node_modules grep for notif|push|fcm|firebase|onesignal matches only the unrelated `safe-push-apply` util; a grep of all of src/ for expo-notifications|getExpoPushToken|pushToken|setNotificationHandler|registerForPushNotifications returns zero matches. app.json:42-68 lists no notifications plugin, and no google-services.json or GoogleService-Info.plist exists under android/.
findings.failure: User B receives a partner request, a trainer request, an @mention or a chat message. Their phone stays silent — no banner, no badge, no sound. The row sits in public.notifications indefinitely. B learns about it only if they independently reopen the app and navigate to the Discover tab, since src/app/(tabs)/discover/index.tsx:54-60 is the only place getUnreadCount() is called and it fires only on that tab's focus. The single realtime channel in the app (src/lib/chat.ts:156) is filtered to one thread_id and only delivers while B is already staring at that exact conversation.
findings.fix: Add expo-notifications and register it in app.json plugins; this is a native module, so it needs a prebuild and a fresh binary (expo run:android / EAS build) — it cannot ship over OTA, and every existing install must update. Supply FCM V1 credentials for Android plus the Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission, and an APNs key with the aps-environment entitlement for iOS. Server side, add an RLS-protected push-token table (owner-writable, client-unreadable) and fire the send from inside public.notify() itself via pg_net or a DB webhook to https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send — notify() is the single point every one of the twelve types passes through. Gate the push behind the same notif_enabled() check that already guards the INSERT, so a type the user switched off does not buzz their phone.

findings.title: Chat deadlocks permanently: one-message-until-reply gate plus zero push means neither side can nudge the other
findings.evidence: messages_gate() raises `wait_for_reply` (errcode 42501) when the sender already has one message in a thread the other side has not answered: `if mine >= 1 then raise exception 'wait_for_reply'`. The trigger messages_one_until_reply is confirmed live on public.messages. The messages_notify trigger writes a 'message' notification row, but as established above nothing delivers that row to the device.
findings.failure: A sends a partner request, B accepts, A opens the thread and sends one message to arrange a time. A is now hard-blocked by messages_gate() from sending anything further. B is never alerted that a message arrived — no push, and the in-app unread badge only refreshes when B happens to open the Discover tab. The thread is stuck forever unless B independently reopens the app. For an app whose core purpose is arranging to meet a training partner at a specific gym at a specific time, the primary flow silently fails.
findings.fix: Ships as part of the push fix above — the 'message' type must reach the device. Until push exists, consider surfacing the unread count on the tab bar rather than only inside Discover, and reconsider whether the one-message gate should hold when the recipient has never opened the thread.

findings.title: Notification settings screen offers switches for two notification types no trigger can ever write
findings.evidence: NOTIF_TYPES includes { type: 'video_like', label: 'Videomu bəyənəndə' } and { type: 'post_like', label: 'Postumu bəyənəndə' } at src/lib/notifications.ts:52-53, and src/app/(tabs)/profile/notifications.tsx:76 renders a live Switch for every entry. But the live pg_trigger listing shows notify triggers on only comment_likes, comments, follows, match_requests, messages, reviews and trainer_requests — there is no trigger on video_likes or post_likes, so no row of either type can ever be produced. The same screen's own footer at src/app/(tabs)/profile/notifications.tsx:101 states «Video və postlara qoyulan bəyənmələr üçün hələ bildiriş yoxdur», directly contradicting the two switches rendered above it, and its stated reason («bəyənmə hazırda yalnız cihazda saxlanılır, ona görə server kimin nəyi bəyəndiyini bilmir») is now false: schema43 created public.video_likes and public.post_likes and src/lib/social.ts:31,56 inserts into both, so the server does know who liked what.
findings.failure: A user opens Parametrlər → Bildirişlər, sees «Videomu bəyənəndə» switched on, and reasonably concludes they will be told when someone likes their video. They never will, because no trigger writes that type. Toggling the switch writes a notif_prefs key that nothing reads. Two rows down, the footer tells them this notification does not exist — so the screen both offers and denies the same feature, and explains it with a reason that stopped being true when schema43 shipped.
findings.fix: Either add the two missing triggers on public.video_likes and public.post_likes calling notify() (both tables and their inserts already exist), or remove the video_like and post_like entries from NOTIF_TYPES until the triggers land. Either way the footer at src/app/(tabs)/profile/notifications.tsx:101 needs correcting — its stated reason no longer matches the schema.

explanation:
CLAIM CONFIRMED — there is no error boundary anywhere in the app. But the second half of the task (naming crash-prone screens) came back largely NEGATIVE, and I want to be equally plain about that.

## 1. The boundary really is absent (proven three ways)

a) `grep -rn "componentDidCatch|getDerivedStateFromError|ErrorBoundary|ErrorUtils|setJSExceptionHandler"` over the repo returns ZERO hits in `src/`. The only hits are `D:\spot\design-handoff\support.js:928` and `D:\spot\design-handoff-v2\fitness-community-app-concept\project\support.js:928` — design-handoff reference material, not app code. `grep -rc "ErrorBoundary" src/` returns nothing at all.

b) There are ZERO class components in `src/` (`grep "extends (React.)?Component|extends PureComponent"` → no output), so no boundary can exist: only a class can be one.

c) No route exports one. expo-router 57.0.14 only wraps a route when the route module exports `ErrorBoundary` — `D:\spot\node_modules\expo-router\build\useScreens.js:141`:
```js
function fromImport(value, { ErrorBoundary, SuspenseFallback, ...component }) {
    ...
    if (ErrorBoundary) {
        const Wrapped = React.forwardRef((props, ref) => {
            ...
            return jsx(Try, { catch: ErrorBoundary, children });
        });
        ...
    }
    ...
    return { default: component.default, SuspenseFallback };   // <-- unwrapped
}
```
`grep "export function ErrorBoundary|export const ErrorBoundary"` across all 14 `_layout.tsx` files and every route → no hits. So the `Try` wrapper (`expo-router/build/views/Try.js`) is never instantiated, and expo-router's own default boundary (`views/ErrorBoundary.js`) is dead code in this build.

## 2. What the user actually sees (React 19.2.3 / RN 0.86.2)

A throw in any screen's render propagates uncaught to the React root. React 19 unmounts the ENTIRE tree — not just the failing screen. Everything in `src/app/_layout.tsx:70-89` goes with it: `GestureHandlerRootView`, `SafeAreaProvider`, the `Stack`, `StatusBar`, and `UiHost` (the global toast/dialog host). So the app cannot even show its own error toast.

`app.json` sets no root window `backgroundColor` — the only colors are the splash (`#E6F4FE`, line 25) and the notification icon (`#208AEF`, line 47). The user is left with the bare default white window: no header, no tab bar, no back affordance, nothing tappable. Force-quitting is the only recovery, and because the fault is in render, returning to the same screen (same tab, or a deep link) throws again immediately. In a release build RN's global `ErrorUtils` handler additionally reports the error as fatal, which on Android typically terminates the process outright.

Note for whoever fixes this: the one-line fix `export { ErrorBoundary } from 'expo-router'` would violate product rule #2. expo-router's built-in boundary hardcodes English — `"Something went wrong"`, `"Error: "`, `"Retry"`, `"Sitemap"` (`node_modules/expo-router/build/views/ErrorBoundary.js:15-30`). SPOT needs its own Azerbaijani boundary.

## 3. The "screens most likely to throw" — I could not find one

I went looking for the unguarded access the claim assumed, and the codebase is systematically defensive. Every single candidate I checked was already guarded:
- `workout/session.tsx:241` `logs[ci]` → guarded by an early return at :400 with a real Azerbaijani empty-state ("Bu günə hərəkət təyin olunmayıb"); the "next" button is bounded by `ci < logs.length - 1` at :567.
- `workout/session.tsx:503` `current.suggestion!.weight` — the one non-null assertion in `src/` — is genuinely safe: `showAccept` (:431-435) requires `!!current.suggestion`, and the `openSet.kg` read on the same line is fenced by `!!openSet &&`.
- `workout/home-session.tsx:41` `plan.moves[idx]` → `if (!move) return null;` at :131.
- `profile/index.tsx:44,269` `weights[0].kg` / `weightDelta.toFixed(1)` → length checks.
- `profile/analytics.tsx:27-28` `reduce` with no seed → fenced by `nonZero.length ?`.

findings.title: No ErrorBoundary anywhere in the app: any render throw unmounts the entire tree to a white screen with nothing tappable
findings.evidence: Zero hits for componentDidCatch/getDerivedStateFromError/ErrorBoundary in src/ (only design-handoff/support.js:928, reference material). Zero class components in src/, so no boundary can exist. No route or _layout exports ErrorBoundary, and expo-router 57.0.14 only wraps a route in its <Try> catcher when the module exports one -- node_modules/expo-router/build/useScreens.js:141 'if (ErrorBoundary) { ... return jsx(Try, {catch: ErrorBoundary}) }' followed by an unwrapped 'return { default: component.default }'. So expo-router's own default boundary (build/views/ErrorBoundary.js) is dead code here. The root tree at src/app/_layout.tsx:70-89 (GestureHandlerRootView > SafeAreaProvider > Stack + UiHost + StatusBar) has no catcher above or below it.
findings.failure: A user on any screen hits a render-time throw -- e.g. a persisted workout lacking an 'exercises' key reaching computeStats (src/store/db.ts:625), which is reachable because both persist configs (src/store/db.ts:353, src/store/appStore.ts:136) declare no version and no migrate while persisting 'workouts' (db.ts:562-572). React 19.2.3 unmounts the WHOLE tree, including UiHost, so the app cannot even raise its own toast. app.json declares no root window backgroundColor (only splash #E6F4FE at line 25), leaving the bare default white window: no header, no tab bar, no back affordance, no control of any kind. Reopening the same tab or deep link re-throws instantly, so force-quitting is the only escape; in a release build RN's ErrorUtils also reports it fatal, which on Android typically kills the process.
findings.fix: Add a custom Azerbaijani error boundary and mount it inside GestureHandlerRootView at src/app/_layout.tsx:71, wrapping the <Stack> so UiHost survives -- a class component with static getDerivedStateFromError, showing an Azerbaijani message plus a 'Yenidən cəhd et' retry that resets state and a 'Ana səhifə' router.replace('/'). Do NOT use the one-line 'export { ErrorBoundary } from "expo-router"': its built-in view hardcodes English ('Something went wrong', 'Error: ', 'Retry', 'Sitemap' -- node_modules/expo-router/build/views/ErrorBoundary.js:15-30) and would violate the Azerbaijani-UI-only rule. Separately, add version + migrate to both persist configs so an old payload cannot reach the unguarded w.exercises reads at db.ts:625, 725, 818 and 829.

findings.title: Admin's «Dayandır» is never read — paused challenges stay joinable in the app

Admin write path: web/admin/src/screens/Challenges.tsx:114 `update({ active: next })`, then audit('challenge_deactivate') and toast «Challenge dayandırıldı» on line 124.
findings.failure: An ops admin pauses «Zallar arası: 100 ton» because the sponsoring gym pulled out. The admin panel flips the badge to PASSİV, writes a challenge_deactivate row with a reason into audit_log, and toasts «Challenge dayandırıldı». On every phone the challenge stays in the «Qoşula bilərsən» list; tapping it opens the detail screen with the reward «Zal reytinqində 1-ci yer» and the «Challenge-ə qoşul» button, which inserts a challenge_members row and toasts success. Both the admin and the user are told something untrue: the admin that the challenge stopped, the user that they joined a running one. Today this is already the live state for two of the three production rows.
findings.fix: Filter on the server in both hooks: `.select('*').eq('active', true)` in useChallenges, and in useChallenge either add the same filter or map `active` and render a stopped state instead of the join button. Add `active: r.active ?? false` to mapChallenge and to the Challenge interface so the flag survives into the client at all.

findings.title: Featured challenge is hardcoded to the seed id 'aug-12'
findings.evidence: `const active = all.find((c) => c.id === 'aug-12') ?? all[0] ?? mockActive;` — the hero card on src/app/challenge/index.tsx:65-90 is chosen by literal string, not by `challenges.active`. The admin create form generates ids as `slug(title)-<Date.now().toString(36).slice(-4)>` (web/admin/src/screens/Challenges.tsx:64,137), so no admin-created id can ever equal 'aug-12'.
findings.failure: An admin pauses aug-12 and activates a freshly created «Sentyabr · 15 məşq». The app still pins the paused August challenge to the top of the screen as the user's active challenge with its progress bar and reward tag, and pushes the real September one down into the «Qoşula bilərsən» row. The admin has no way to change which challenge is featured, ever.
findings.fix: Pick the hero from data, not from a literal: `all.find(c => c.active)` (after adding `active` to the mapper), falling back to an honest empty state when nothing is active rather than to `mockActive`.

findings.title: «Avqust · 12 məşq» is live in September and its progress silently reset on the 1st
findings.evidence: Live row (queried 2026-09-08): id='aug-12', active=true, title='Avqust · 12 məşq', description='Avqust ayında 12 məşq tamamla…'. `computeChallengeProgress` builds `monthStart` from `new Date()` with `setDate(1)` and counts only `w.at >= monthStart` (db.ts:1029-1040). The challenges table has no starts_at/ends_at column at all (verified against information_schema.columns), so nothing can ever expire it.
findings.failure: A user who logged 11 of the required 12 workouts during August opens the Challenge tab on 1 September. The card still reads «Avqust · 12 məşq» and «Avqust ayında 12 məşq tamamla», but the bar now reads 0 / 12 and the caption switches to «Hələ başlamamısan — ilk məşqini qeyd et.» Their August work is gone from a challenge that still claims to be about August, and the September workouts they log now accrue to an August target that can never be settled.
findings.fix: Add real `starts_at`/`ends_at` timestamptz columns to public.challenges, scope `computeChallengeProgress` to `[starts_at, ends_at)` instead of the current calendar month, and have the client render an ended challenge as ended rather than as a zeroed live one.

findings.title: Reward «1 aylıq üzvlük» is displayed with no mechanism anywhere that can award it
findings.evidence: `reward` is rendered at src/app/challenge/index.tsx:70 (volt tag on the hero card) and [id].tsx:82 («Mükafat»). Grepping src/ and supabase/ for reward/winner/qalib finds no other consumer: no winners table, no award RPC, no admin action, no notification. The same screen already admits it cannot rank ([id].tsx:106) or count down ([id].tsx:113), and `select count(*) from challenge_members` is 0, so there is no participant set to judge either.
findings.failure: A user reads «1 aylıq üzvlük» on the hero card, joins, and logs 12 workouts. Nothing in the app or the admin panel can detect that they finished — there is no end date to finish by, no ranking, no completion check and no award path — so the month of membership is never issued and the user is never told why. findings.fix: Either stop rendering `reward` until a settlement path exists (an end date, a completion check, and an admin award action that writes a record the user can see), or reword it in the UI as a non-binding description and say plainly that winners are chosen off-platform by the gym.

findings.title: The 7-day strip counts check-ins while the counter directly above it ignores them
findings.evidence: `useLast7Days` lights a cell from `[...workouts, ...checkIns]` (index.tsx:28), and the strip is captioned «Son 7 gün» (index.tsx:83-89). Check-ins are the server-verified signal (src/app/(tabs)/workout/checkin.tsx:217-240 writes locally only after the server accepts).
findings.failure: A user does a GPS-verified QR check-in at their gym every day for a week. On one card they see all seven day cells lit volt under «Son 7 gün», and directly above them «0 / 12» with the caption «Hələ başlamamısan — ilk məşqini qeyd et.» The same screen tells them they trained seven days and that they have not started. CONFIRMED, with one narrowing on the `days` half.

THE PRE-FILLED FIELDS (D:\spot\src\store\appStore.ts, `emptyProfile`, lines 117-133):
```
125	  level: 'Orta',            // LEVELS[1] of ['Başlanğıc','Orta','İrəli']
127	  days: [0, 2, 4],          // DAYS indexes -> 'B.e', 'Çər', 'Cüm'
128	  timeSlot: 'Axşam 17–21',  // TIME_SLOTS[2]
```
Every other field is honestly empty (`name:''`, `age:null`, `homeGymId:null`, `goals:[]`, `types:[]`, `bio:''`, `priceFrom:null`) and each carries a comment explaining why. Three fields break that discipline.

DO THEY REACH THE SERVER WHEN THE USER SKIPS? Two of the three, yes, verbatim. `toDbPatch()` (appStore.ts:97-115) sends them unconditionally:
```
109	    level: p.level,
112	    time_slot: p.timeSlot,
```
There is no "only if chosen" guard, unlike the one right above it for `username` (line 105). `saveProfile()` (appStore.ts:307-344) calls `updateMyProfile({ ...toDbPatch(s.profile), ... })` with no filtering.

`days` is the exception: `profiles` has no `days` column (verified against the live DB — information_schema returns level, time_slot, goals, types, home_gym_id, age but no `days`), and `toDbPatch` omits it. So the invented [0,2,4] never reaches Postgres. It still drives local surfaces (see finding 3).

THE SKIP PATH IS REAL. `OnboardingScaffold` renders «Keç» whenever `onSkip` is passed. goal.tsx:24, level.tsx:23 and schedule.tsx:23 all pass `onSkip={next}`. So goal -> level -> schedule can all be skipped in three taps. Step 4 (gym) and step 5 (profile: name/handle/age) have no skip, so the person does end up with a real name — which means `saveProfile()` passes its `if (!get().profile.name.trim()) return 'local'` guard at line 310 and the write goes out. A skipper's `profiles` row lands with level='Orta' and time_slot='Axşam 17–21' that they never touched.

THE SECOND HALF — "Eyni saat / Eyni səviyyə" — ALSO CONFIRMED. src/lib/api.ts `compatibility()`: `slotMatch('Axşam 17–21','Axşam 17–21')` returns 1 -> line 491 `reasons.push('Eyni saat')`; `levelProximity('Orta','Orta')` returns 1 -> line 497 `reasons.push('Eyni səviyyə')`. Both land in `matchReasons` (api.ts:546), are classified as positives by `splitReasons()` (PartnerRow.tsx:56-67, neither string matches MISMATCH_RE), and render as green chips. Score impact: `raw = 30*gym + 25*slot + 15*level + ...` (api.ts:514), so 40 of 100 points come from data nobody entered. Two skippers see each other at 40% with two green reasons.

A COLLATERAL CASUALTY: `canCompare()` (api.ts:520-523) returns true if `!!me.level` — since level is never empty after this app writes it, that guard can never return false, so the deliberate «hesablanmadı» path (mapPartner comment, api.ts:527-533) is unreachable for any profile this client saved. Same for `schedule.tsx:23 nextDisabled={days.length === 0}` — with the default [0,2,4] the "you must pick days" gate is dead on arrival.

WHY THE COMPARISON CODE ITSELF IS INNOCENT: `toLevel('')` returns null (src/data/types.ts:16-23), `levelProximity` then returns 0 -> `mismatches.push('Səviyyə göstərilməyib')` (api.ts:499), and `slotMatch(null, …)` returns 0 -> «Vaxt göstərilməyib» (api.ts:493). The honest branches already exist and are already written. Only the client-side fabrication stops them from ever firing.

LIVE DB: only 1 profile row exists, and it does hold level='Orta' + time_slot='Axşam 17–21'. n=1 proves nothing statistically; the code path is the proof.

findings.title: Onboarding pre-selects level 'Orta' and slot «Axşam 17–21» and writes them to the server as the user's own choice
findings.evidence: emptyProfile (appStore.ts:117-133) sets `level: 'Orta'` (line 125) and `timeSlot: 'Axşam 17–21'` (line 128) while every neighbouring field is honestly empty. toDbPatch() sends both unconditionally: line 109 `level: p.level,` and line 112 `time_slot: p.timeSlot,` — no "only when chosen" guard, unlike the one for `username` on line 105. saveProfile() (line 328) spreads toDbPatch straight into updateMyProfile(). level.tsx:23 and schedule.tsx:23 both pass `onSkip={next}`, so those two steps are skippable in two taps.
findings.failure: A new user taps «Keç» on the Səviyyə step and «Keç» on the Cədvəl step, then fills in name/handle/age (step 5 has no skip) and finishes. Their public profiles row is written with level='Orta' and time_slot='Axşam 17–21'. Every partner card, filter and compatibility score across the app now treats those as declared facts. They never made either choice.
findings.fix: Start empty: `level: ''`, `timeSlot: ''` in emptyProfile, and drop the pre-selection from level.tsx:28 / schedule.tsx:42 (the SelectCards already render unselected when the value is ''). Then send null rather than a guess in toDbPatch: `level: p.level || null,` and `time_slot: p.timeSlot || null,`. No downstream change is needed — compatibility() already produces «Səviyyə göstərilməyib» (api.ts:499) and «Vaxt göstərilməyib» (api.ts:493) for nulls, and toLevel('') already returns null (data/types.ts:18).

findings.title: «Eyni saat» and «Eyni səviyyə» are shown as match reasons for two people who never chose either
findings.evidence: compatibility(): line 490 `const slot = slotMatch(me.time_slot, other.time_slot);` then 491 `if (slot >= 1) reasons.push('Eyni saat');`; line 496 `const level = levelProximity(me.level, other.level);` then 497 `if (level >= 1) reasons.push('Eyni səviyyə');`. Both defaults are identical for every skipper, so both fire with value 1. They enter matchReasons (line 546), survive splitReasons() as positives (PartnerRow.tsx:60,64 — neither string matches MISMATCH_RE) and render as green chips (PartnerRow.tsx:104-108). The score formula on line 514 is `30*gym + 25*slot + 15*level + 15*goal + 10*type`, so slot+level contribute 40 of 100 points.
findings.failure: Two users who both skipped the Səviyyə and Cədvəl steps open Yoldaşlar. Each sees the other at 40% uyğun with the green chips «Eyni saat» and «Eyni səviyyə». Neither ever told the app when they train or how experienced they are. The app is asserting a measured agreement over two invented constants.
findings.fix: Fixed by finding 1 — stop fabricating the values at the source. With nulls on the server, slotMatch and levelProximity both return 0 and the same code honestly pushes «Vaxt göstərilməyib» / «Səviyyə göstərilməyib» into mismatches instead.

findings.title: Default days [0,2,4] become an invented weekly target in Analitika and the shared report
findings.evidence: emptyProfile line 127 `days: [0, 2, 4]`. This one never reaches Postgres — the live `profiles` table has no `days` column (confirmed via information_schema) and toDbPatch omits it — but analytics.tsx:16 reads `const plannedDays = useAppStore((s) => s.profile.days.length);` and line 39 `const target = plannedDays > 0 ? plannedDays : 0;` feeds the consistency percentage on line 40 and the Share text on line 46 (`/ ${target} planlanmış`). The comment on line 38 claims "Denominator is the user's OWN weekly plan from onboarding — never an invented target", which is exactly what it is for anyone who skipped. schedule.tsx:23 `nextDisabled={days.length === 0}` can also never fire, so the gate meant to force a real choice is dead.
findings.failure: A user who skipped the Cədvəl step trains twice this week, opens Analitika and reads «67% ardıcıllıq», then shares a report saying «Bu həftə: 2 məşq / 3 planlanmış». They never planned 3 days.
findings.fix: `days: []` in emptyProfile. analytics.tsx already handles target===0 correctly (consistency becomes null, the share line drops the «/ N planlanmış» clause), and schedule.tsx:23's nextDisabled guard starts working as intended.

findings.title: A partner whose level the server does not hold is rendered as «Orta»
findings.evidence: mapPartner(): line 539 comment "Never surface a raw stored value — see toLevel", line 540 `level: toLevel(p.level) ?? 'Orta',`. toLevel returns null for an absent or unrecognised value (data/types.ts:16-23) precisely so the field can be omitted — its own doc comment says "an unrecognised value returns null so the field is simply omitted rather than guessed at" — and the ?? then guesses anyway. PartnerRow.tsx:101 prints it: `{[partner.level, partner.usualTime].filter(Boolean).join(' · ')}`, and the filter(Boolean) that exists to drop the empty case never gets an empty value.
findings.failure: A profile row with level=null (a user from before this field existed, or one created outside onboarding) shows up in Yoldaşlar as «Elvin, 27 · Orta · Axşam 17–21». The app states an experience level that no row anywhere contains.
findings.fix: `level: toLevel(p.level) ?? '',` — PartnerRow.tsx:101's `.filter(Boolean)` then omits the segment, which is what both that filter and toLevel's null return were written for. Check the Partner type at data/types.ts allows '' (usualTime already uses the same `?? ''` pattern on api.ts:544).
