WHAT AN OWNER CAN READ TODAY, for every profile whose `home_gym_id` is their gym — all 24 columns above.

Against the design matrix at D:\spot\design-handoff\README.md:77-92 ("İcazə matrisi", gym_admin column):
- INSIDE the line: id, name, avatar_url, age, bio, home_gym_id, created_at (+ check-in frequency, which comes from check_ins).
- CROSSING the line: `level`, `goals`, `time_slot` — README.md:82 marks "Səviyyə, məqsəd, qrafik" as ✗ for gym_admin, explicitly. Also `status`, `status_reason` (a moderator's free-text sanction reason), `status_until`, `user_id` (the raw auth uid, a cross-table join key), `notif_prefs`, `last_active_at`, `visibility`, `show_in_gym_list`, `username`, `types`, `role`, `specialty`, `price_from`.

The hardest red line (README.md:92 — weight, workout detail, chat archive) is NOT crossed: profiles has no weight/workout/message columns, and no policy grants an owner access to those tables. So the claim is right about the matrix, not about the red line.

TWO EXTRA HOLES the same policy opens, because its qual mentions neither guard that `profiles_read` uses:
1. `show_in_gym_list` is ignored. A member who turned off "Zalda göründüyümü göstər" — promised at D:\spot\src\app\(tabs)\profile\privacy.tsx:222 with "Söndürsən, zalın siyahısında heç görünmürsən" — is still fully readable by the owner. The roster masks them to "Anonim üzv" purely in JavaScript (D:\spot\src\lib\gymOwner.tsx:329-335) AFTER D:\spot\src\lib\roles.ts:285-288 has already pulled their real `name`, `level` and `goals` over the wire. D:\spot\supabase\schema38_blocks_and_visibility.sql:131-132 states this was left deliberately: "the gym owner's existing read of their own members stays: policies are OR'd and profiles_gym_owner_read is untouched."
2. `blocked_between` is ignored. Blocking the gym owner does not hide you from them.

The roster query itself asks for the forbidden columns: D:\spot\src\lib\roles.ts:287 selects `id,name,level,goals`. Nothing under D:\spot\src\app\gym\ renders level or goals (grep is clean), so this is not visible in the UI — but the data reaches the owner's device, and D:\spot\src\app\gym\members.tsx:230 prints a lock icon over the sentence "Zal admini ... yalnız check-in tezliyini və üzvlük statusunu [görür]", which is a guarantee the server does not enforce.

SCOPE HONESTY: the live DB is pre-launch — `select count(*) from gyms where owner_id is not null` returns 0, and 1 profile has a home_gym_id, 0 hidden, 0 sanctioned. So no end-to-end demonstration with real rows was possible and nobody is exposed today; the finding is structural and deterministic from the policy + grant text, which I read live. I did not run any DDL/DML.

Note for whoever fixes this: the column grants here are already column-level, so a plain `revoke select (status, status_reason, status_until, notif_prefs) on public.profiles from anon, authenticated` is enough — the table-level-GRANT-beats-column-REVOKE trap does not bite, because schema9_found_gaps.sql:148 already did the table-level revoke first.

findings.title: profiles_gym_owner_read is a whole-row policy: the gym owner reads level, goals, schedule, moderation status and the auth uid of every member
findings.evidence: Live pg_policies: policyname=profiles_gym_owner_read, cmd=SELECT, permissive, qual=((home_gym_id IS NOT NULL) AND owns_gym(home_gym_id)). RLS restricts rows, never columns. Live column_privileges for grantee 'authenticated' SELECT on public.profiles = age, avatar_url, bio, created_at, gender, goals, home_gym_id, id, last_active_at, level, name, notif_prefs, price_from, role, show_in_gym_list, specialty, status, status_reason, status_until, time_slot, types, user_id, username, visibility (only `phone` withheld). Grants are per-role, so this policy hands the owner all 24 columns. design-handoff/README.md:82 marks "Səviyyə, məqsəd, qrafik" (level, goal, schedule) as ✗ for gym_admin.
findings.failure: A gym owner signs in, opens the network tab or calls the REST endpoint their own app already uses — GET /rest/v1/profiles?home_gym_id=eq.<their gym>&select=* minus phone — and gets, for every member: level, goals, time_slot, gender, age, bio, username, user_id (auth uid), last_active_at, visibility, plus status/status_reason/status_until. The permission matrix promises them a name, an avatar and check-in frequency.
findings.fix: Drop profiles_gym_owner_read and serve the roster from a SECURITY DEFINER function (set row_security = off) that returns only id, name, avatar_url, show_in_gym_list, created_at joined to the check-in aggregates — the same shape getGymRoster already builds. If the policy must stay, put the owner path behind a column-limited view instead, since no RLS policy can narrow columns.

findings.title: The gym-owner policy ignores show_in_gym_list, so "Anonim üzv" is a client-side costume over a name the server already handed over
findings.evidence: profiles_gym_owner_read's qual is (home_gym_id IS NOT NULL AND owns_gym(home_gym_id)) — it never mentions show_in_gym_list, and permissive policies are OR'd, so it overrides the show_in_gym_list guard that profiles_read carries. src/lib/roles.ts:287 fetches `id,name,level,goals` for the whole roster; only afterwards does gymOwner.tsx:315 fetch show_in_gym_list and gymOwner.tsx:329-335 blank the name to 'Anonim üzv'. supabase/schema38_blocks_and_visibility.sql:131-132 records the decision to leave it: "profiles_gym_owner_read is untouched".
findings.failure: A member turns off "Zalda göründüyümü göstər" — the footer at src/app/(tabs)/profile/privacy.tsx:222 promises "Söndürsən, zalın siyahısında heç görünmürsən". The owner's roster shows a '?' avatar and 'Anonim üzv', while the same screen's own HTTP response already contains that member's real name, level and goals; the owner reads it in the network log or by querying profiles directly. The app states a privacy guarantee it did not obtain.
findings.fix: Enforce anonymity server-side: the roster RPC must return NULL for name/avatar_url when show_in_gym_list is false, rather than shipping the real values and masking them in JS. Then the toggle means what privacy.tsx:222 says.

findings.title: The gym-owner policy also bypasses blocked_between, so blocking the gym owner does not hide you from them
findings.evidence: profiles_read's qual carries `(COALESCE(show_in_gym_list, true) AND (NOT blocked_between(id, my_profile_id())))`. profiles_gym_owner_read's qual is `((home_gym_id IS NOT NULL) AND owns_gym(home_gym_id))` — no blocked_between term at all. Permissive policies are OR'd, so the block is defeated for anyone who owns the member's home gym.
findings.failure: A member is harassed by a gym owner and blocks them. Because the member's home_gym_id still points at that gym, the owner keeps full read access to the member's profile row — name, avatar, age, gender, bio, level, goals — and the member's block silently does nothing against the one person it was aimed at.
findings.fix: Add `and not blocked_between(id, my_profile_id())` to the owner's read path (or to the replacement roster RPC), matching the guard profiles_read already uses.

findings.title: status_reason — a moderator's free-text sanction note — is SELECT-granted to anon and authenticated, so the gym owner (and everyone else) can read why a member was banned
findings.evidence: Live column_privileges confirm SELECT on status, status_reason, status_until is held by both anon and authenticated. status_reason is the free-text reason an admin types when sanctioning: web/admin/src/screens/Moderation.tsx:194 and web/admin/src/screens/Users.tsx:238 write `{ status, status_reason: reason, status_until }`. schema18_enforcement.sql:38 declares these columns off-limits — but that file only revoked UPDATE (schema18:30), never SELECT.
findings.failure: Any signed-in user — and specifically the gym owner, for whom profiles_gym_owner_read also lifts the show_in_gym_list gate — issues GET /rest/v1/profiles?select=name,status,status_reason and reads the moderator's private note explaining why a member was muted, suspended or banned.
findings.fix: revoke select (status, status_reason, status_until, notif_prefs) on public.profiles from anon, authenticated. The table-level revoke at schema9_found_gaps.sql:148 already ran, so a column-level revoke takes effect here. Expose only the derived boolean via the existing is_sanctioned() (schema18_enforcement.sql:48) and keep the reason behind an admin RPC.

explanation:
CONFIRMED, with the scope sharpened. I sampled 20+ screens across all five tabs plus the gym-owner and trainer panels. The claim's three parts hold as follows:

**(a) No skeletons — 100% true app-wide.** `grep -rn "Skeleton\|shimmer" src/` returns zero hits. The design handoff explicitly requires them: `design-handoff/README.md:296` ("Yüklənmə: skeleton (spinner deyil)"), `design-handoff/INTERACTIONS.md:693` (12.2 Skeleton, "10 s-dan çox çəkərsə → xəta vəziyyəti"), and `design-handoff/SPOT iOS App.dc.html:3182` ("hər xəta səbəbi izah edir və təkrar cəhd düyməsi verir"). Nothing in the app implements this. There is no retry button on any failed read either.

**(b) No offline banner — 100% true app-wide.** `@react-native-community/netinfo` is not in `package.json` and `NetInfo` appears nowhere in `src/`. The app has no way to know it is offline. Every string containing "offline" in the codebase means `!hasSupabaseConfig` (a build-time flag: this build has no backend), not "the device lost its connection" — e.g. `src/app/chat/requests.tsx:36`.

**(c) Errors rendered as empty states — true for a large, specific set; false for others.** The root cause is that the shared data layer has no failure channel at all: `src/lib/focusFetch.ts:60` (`.catch(() => {})`), `src/lib/hooks.ts:29` and `src/lib/hooks.ts:46` (both `.catch(() => {})`). The API layer below them *does* throw properly (`src/lib/api.ts:313`, `:598`, `:613` all `if (error) throw error`), so the error reaches the hook and is then discarded. A consumer receives the identical value for "still loading", "server returned zero rows", and "the read failed".

Screens that ALREADY handle this correctly and which I am deliberately NOT reporting: `src/app/chat/requests.tsx` (Phase = loading|ready|offline|error), `src/app/chat/index.tsx:83` (`threadsFailed`), `src/app/(tabs)/profile/saved.tsx:36` (`'failed'` sentinel), `src/app/gym/index.tsx:54` (per-source `errors` map, failure drawn as «—» not 0), `src/app/gym/members.tsx:44` and `src/app/gym/reviews.tsx:27` (both with the comment "that is NOT the same as no reviews/members yet"), `src/app/trainer/index.tsx`, `src/app/trainer/chat.tsx`, `src/app/trainer/student/[id].tsx:102` (offline|failed|not-found three-way), `src/app/(tabs)/workout/program/[id].tsx:72` (probe pending|failed|missing), `src/app/(tabs)/workout/index.tsx:70` (`assignedFailed`), and `src/app/(tabs)/profile/notifications.tsx`. Local-only screens (`profile/history.tsx`, `profile/achievements.tsx`, `trainer/programs.tsx`, `challenge/gyms.tsx`, `gym/classes.tsx`) read from the device store and are not affected.

What remains broken is the entire **Kəşf (Discover)** tab and both lists on the **Feed** tab. One nuance on the Feed: the earlier fix covered the comment counts and like state (`src/app/(tabs)/feed/index.tsx:63`, `:83`, `:250` — all correctly refuse to claim a zero they did not measure), but the list-level empty state was never touched. Because `src/data/feed.ts:49` and `:56` are now `[]` (the fabricated seed content was correctly removed), the seed fallback no longer masks anything: a failed feed read produces exactly the same empty array as a successful one, and the user is told nothing has ever been posted. `playersReady` at `src/app/(tabs)/feed/index.tsx:209` is a native-player mount tick, not a data-load flag, so it does not gate this.

The worst single instance is `src/app/(tabs)/discover/gym/[id].tsx:71`: `load().catch(() => setLoaded(true))` — a thrown network error is explicitly converted into "loaded", after which line 666 tests `reviewsLoaded && totalReviews === 0` and prints "Hələ rəy yoxdur". The failure path is written out in code as success.

This violates product rule 3 (radical honesty): "An error must never render as 'nothing here yet'."

findings.title: Shared fetch layer discards every error, giving consumers no way to tell failure from empty
findings.evidence: `useFocusFetch` does `loadRef.current().then(...).catch(() => {})` at src/lib/focusFetch.ts:60 and returns a bare `T` — no loading flag, no error. `useList` (src/lib/hooks.ts:29) and `useOne` (src/lib/hooks.ts:46) do the same `.catch(() => {})`. The API layer beneath them throws correctly (src/lib/api.ts:313 `if (error) throw error`, :598, :613), so a real error arrives and is dropped. For hooks whose fallback is an empty array (`NO_TRAINERS`/`NO_PARTNERS`, src/lib/hooks.ts:57-58) or null, the value returned after a failed read is byte-identical to the value returned after a genuinely empty result and to the value returned while still loading.
findings.failure: Device loses connectivity, or RLS/PostgREST returns an error. `getPartnersAtGym` throws, useFocusFetch swallows it, the hook returns `NO_PARTNERS` ([]). Every one of the eight consumer screens below renders its 'there is nobody here yet' copy. The user is told a factual claim about the world that the app never obtained.
findings.fix: Change the return type to a discriminated state, e.g. `{ status: 'loading' | 'ready' | 'failed'; data: T }`, set `status: 'failed'` inside the catch, and keep the last known-good `data` alongside it. The pattern is already proven in this codebase at src/app/chat/requests.tsx:36 and src/app/gym/members.tsx:44; this just lifts it into the shared hooks so consumers can branch on it.

findings.title: Feed renders a failed video read as «Hələ video yoxdur»
findings.evidence: `videos` comes from `useFeedVideos()` (src/lib/hooks.ts:341), a `useFocusFetch` whose fallback is `mockVideos` — and `src/data/feed.ts:49` is now `export const feedVideos: FeedVideo[] = [];`. So the seed no longer masks a failure. The `ListEmptyComponent` at line 320-327 has no phase check: line 321 prints «Hələ video yoxdur» and line 323 «Bu feed-də hələ heç nə paylaşılmayıb. Birinci sən ol — texnika videonu yüklə.» The `playersReady` gate at line 209 is set by `afterTransition` (line 212), i.e. a native-player mount tick, not a data-load flag. Note the counts/likes on this same screen WERE fixed (lines 63, 83, 250) — the list-level state was not.
findings.failure: User opens SPOT on a train with no signal. The `feed_videos` select fails, useFocusFetch swallows it, `videos` is []. The home screen of the app states that nobody has ever posted a video to SPOT and invites the user to be the first — while the real feed is full of content.
findings.fix: Thread the fetch status out of `useFeedVideos` and branch the ListEmptyComponent three ways: a skeleton grid while loading, «Videolar yüklənmədi — bağlantını yoxla» plus a retry button on failure, and the current copy only on a confirmed empty result.

findings.title: Community feed renders a failed post read as «Hələ post yoxdur»
findings.evidence: The «Zalım» list's `ListEmptyComponent` (lines 726-739) tests only `visible.length === 0`. Its source `useCommunityPosts()` (src/lib/hooks.ts:369) falls back to `mockPosts`, and `src/data/feed.ts:56` is `export const communityPosts: CommunityPost[] = [];`. Line 730 prints «{gym} zalında hələ post yoxdur» and line 735 «İcmada hələ heç nə paylaşılmayıb. Birinci sən ol.»
findings.failure: The `community_posts` select fails. The user is told their gym's community board is empty and is offered «İlk postu yaz» — when in fact the board has posts that simply could not be fetched.
findings.fix: Same three-way branch as the video list; keep the last successfully-read posts on screen rather than clearing to empty.

findings.title: Gym detail marks a thrown review-read error as successfully loaded, then prints «Hələ rəy yoxdur»
findings.evidence: Line 71 is literally `load().catch(() => setLoaded(true));` — the error handler sets the loaded flag. Inside `load` (line 57) the destructure is `const { data } = await supabase.from('reviews')...`, dropping `error`, so a PostgREST error also yields `data === null` → `setRows([])` → `setLoaded(true)` at line 67. Line 666 then tests `reviewsLoaded && totalReviews === 0` and renders line 671 «Hələ rəy yoxdur — ilk rəyi sən yaz.» The screen also prints «{totalReviews} rəy» at line 360 and an `avgRating` computed at line 291 from that same empty array.
findings.failure: The reviews query fails for a gym that has 40 reviews averaging 4.6. The gym page shows «Hələ rəy yoxdur» and a 0 review count, and invites the user to write the first review. A prospective member reads this as a verdict on the gym.
findings.fix: Capture `error` from the destructure, add a `failed` state alongside `loaded`, and set `failed` (not `loaded`) in the catch on line 71 — mirroring src/app/gym/reviews.tsx:33-41, which already does exactly this for the owner-side view of the same table.

findings.title: Gym detail shows a failed trainer and member read as an empty gym
findings.evidence: Line 541 tests `gymTrainers.length === 0` and line 542 renders «Bu zalda hələ SPOT-da qeydiyyatdan keçmiş müəllim yoxdur.» `gymTrainers` is `useTrainersForGym(id)` (line 128), a `useList` with `NO_TRAINERS` fallback and `.catch(() => {})`. Identically, line 553 tests `members.length === 0` and line 554 renders «Bu zalda hələ SPOT istifadəçisi yoxdur. Birinci sən ol — check-in et.» — `members` is `usePartnersForGym(id)` (line 127), backed by `getPartnersAtGym`, which throws at src/lib/api.ts:598.
findings.failure: The profiles/trainers query fails on a busy gym's page. Both tabs claim the gym has zero SPOT trainers and zero SPOT users, and the «Üzvlər» tab tells the user to be the first to check in at a gym where dozens already have.
findings.fix: Branch on the fetch status once the hooks expose it; show a skeleton row set while loading and «Siyahı yüklənmədi — yenidən cəhd et» with a retry on failure.

findings.title: Kəşf trainer and partner lists render a failed read as «Hələ müəllim yoxdur» / «hələ uyğun yoldaş yoxdur»
findings.evidence: Line 318 tests only `visibleTrainers.length === 0`; line 319 renders «Hələ müəllim yoxdur. Zalını seç — müəllimlər orada görünəcək.» Source is `useTrainers()` (line 79 → src/lib/hooks.ts:225), fallback `NO_TRAINERS` = []. Line 394 does the same for `visiblePartners`, rendering line 400 «Bu zalda hələ uyğun yoldaş yoxdur. Başqa zal seç və ya profilini tamamla.» The contrast is on the same screen: the «Saxlanılanlar» sub-block at lines 358-378 already implements loading/error/ready properly, so this is an inconsistency within one file.
findings.failure: The `trainers` select fails. The Müəllimlər tab says no trainers exist on SPOT at all and blames the user's gym choice; the Yoldaşlar tab says the user's gym has no compatible partners and suggests they change gyms or fix their profile — three false pieces of advice derived from a network error.
findings.fix: Apply the same `savedPhase` pattern already present at src/app/(tabs)/discover/index.tsx:358-378 to the two main lists.

findings.title: Trainer detail claims «Müəllim tapılmadı» on a failed read, and flashes it during every normal load
findings.evidence: Line 39 `const trainer = useTrainer(id)` → `useOne<Trainer>(null, ...)` at src/lib/hooks.ts:270, whose initial state is `null` and whose `.catch(() => {})` (src/lib/hooks.ts:46) leaves it `null`. Line 57 `if (!trainer)` then renders line 64 «Müəllim tapılmadı.» with a «Geri» button. There is no pending state, so this is shown on the first render of every successful load too. `src/app/(tabs)/workout/program/[id].tsx:72` shows the correct three-way handling (`probe === 'pending' ? 'Yüklənir…' : probe === 'failed' ? 'Proqram yüklənmədi' : 'Proqram tapılmadı'`) for the identical situation.
findings.failure: A user taps a trainer from search on a weak connection. The page states the trainer does not exist and offers only a back button — a claim about a real, verified coach's existence that the app never established. Even on a good connection the 'does not exist' screen flashes before the profile paints.
findings.fix: Copy the `probe` pattern from src/app/(tabs)/workout/program/[id].tsx:66-72 — pending → «Yüklənir…», failed → «Müəllim yüklənmədi» with retry, only a confirmed null → «Müəllim tapılmadı».

findings.title: Reservation screen claims «Müəllim tapılmadı» on a failed read
findings.evidence: Line 37 `const trainer = useTrainer(id)` — same `useOne` null-fallback, error-swallowing hook. Line 79 `if (!trainer)` renders line 90 «Müəllim tapılmadı.» with no pending or failed branch.
findings.failure: User taps «Rezervasiya» on a trainer's page while the connection drops. The booking screen states the trainer does not exist, dead-ending a flow that was one tap from completing, with no retry offered.
findings.fix: Same pending/failed/missing split as the trainer detail screen.

findings.title: Match screen claims «Bu yoldaş tapılmadı» on a failed read
findings.evidence: Line 85 `const partner = usePartner(id ?? '')` → src/lib/hooks.ts:216, a `useFocusFetch` with a `null` fallback whose catch is src/lib/focusFetch.ts:60. Line 154 `if (!partner || !id)` renders line 158 «Bu yoldaş tapılmadı. Siyahıya qayıt.» No loading or failed branch. (Note line 280 in the same file DOES distinguish a missing request honestly — «Bu təklif serverdə tapılmadı» — so the file is inconsistent with itself.)
findings.failure: User taps an accepted partner to propose a session; the `profiles` read fails. The screen says the partner was not found and sends them back to the list, implying the person deleted their account or hid their profile.
findings.fix: Add the pending/failed states and keep the user on the screen with a retry instead of asserting the partner is gone.

findings.title: Partner card deck reports a failed read as «Hamısını gördün»
findings.evidence: `usePartnerDeck(gymId)` (line 21 import; src/lib/hooks.ts:210) returns `NO_PARTNERS` = [] after a swallowed failure. `emptyKind` at line 108 has exactly four values — 'cap' | 'filter' | 'gate' | 'done' — and no failure value, so an empty deck from a failed read falls through to `'done'`, rendering line 238 «Hamısını gördün» and line 247 «Bu zalda cavab vermədiyin yoldaş qalmadı. Yeni adam qoşulanda burada görünəcək.» The file's own comment at line 226 says 'Four different reasons the deck is empty, and the user is told which one' — the fifth reason is missing.
findings.failure: The partner query fails. The deck tells the user they have already swiped through everyone at their gym and there is nobody left to answer — a definitive, false statement about a list the app could not read.
findings.fix: Add a fifth `emptyKind` of 'failed' driven by the hook's status and give it «Kartlar yüklənmədi» plus a retry.

findings.title: Weekly picks screen reports a failed read as «Bu həftə üçün hələ uyğun təklif yoxdur»
findings.evidence: Line 30 `const all = usePartnersForGym(homeGymId ?? '')` — same empty-fallback, error-swallowing chain. Line 79 `if (!top)` renders line 84 «Bu həftə üçün hələ uyğun təklif yoxdur. Profilini tamamla — uyğun adam çıxan kimi burada görünəcək.»
findings.failure: The partner read fails. The screen tells the user the matching algorithm found nobody suitable for them this week and blames their incomplete profile — a personal, discouraging judgement produced entirely by a dropped network error.
findings.fix: Branch on the hook status; on failure say the suggestions could not be loaded and offer a retry rather than attributing the emptiness to the user's profile.

explanation:
CONFIRMED, and worse than claimed. The day-pass flow is a write-only feature: the app inserts a row, prints a code on screen, and then nothing in the product — not the member, not the gym, not the admin — can ever read that code again or change the row.

What the code actually does:
- `src/lib/api.ts:794-813` `buyDayPass()` — generates `Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8).toUpperCase()` (api.ts:797), computes `expires_at` from the *device* clock (`end.setHours(23,59,59,0)`, api.ts:798-799), inserts `status:'active'` and returns the code to the caller. That is the entire server interaction.
- `src/app/(tabs)/discover/gym/[id].tsx:170` holds the returned pass in `useState` only. Grep confirms nothing persists it (no `dayPass` in `src/store`), and there is no "my passes" screen.
- The ONLY two statements in the whole client that touch `day_passes` are that INSERT (api.ts:801) and `getGymDayPasses` (src/lib/roles.ts:356-369), which does `.select('id')` and returns a *count*. No `.eq('code'` exists anywhere in `src` or `web/admin`.

Live database (project oezzgcumwprpoqekmlop, read-only SELECTs):
- `select count(*) ... from public.day_passes` → total 6, status active 6, used 0, expired 0, refunded 0, **active_but_past 6**. Every row is still 'active' with an `expires_at` between 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-01 — 7 to 8 days ago.
- Full listing: iron-bay was issued TWO passes on the same day one second apart (29AL0H 10:35:15, BN6UN7 10:35:16), which is what "no guard" looks like in practice.
- Catalog: `day_passes` has no triggers, no unique index on `code`, no unique on (user_id, gym_id, day) — only `day_passes_pkey` and `day_passes_status_idx (status, purchased_at desc)`. `cron.job` does not exist (pg_cron is not installed; extensions are plpgsql, pg_stat_statements, uuid-ossp, pgcrypto, supabase_vault, postgis). The only function whose body mentions the table is `admin_dashboard`, and it only reads.
- Policies: `dp_user_insert [INSERT] CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id)`, `dp_user_read [SELECT] (auth.uid()=user_id OR is_admin)`, `dp_owner_read [SELECT] owns_gym(gym_id)`, `dp_admin_update [UPDATE] admin_at_least(auth.uid(),'ops')`. There is no owner UPDATE policy, so a gym could not mark a pass used even if a screen existed.
- Bonus, proven by execution: `select public.admin_dashboard();` → `ERROR: 42703: column "commission" does not exist`. The live function body still contains `'revenue_commission', (select coalesce(sum(commission),0) from public.day_passes ...)` even though `schema27_trust_columns.sql:194` dropped the column. The whole admin Dashboard is therefore dead, and a revenue-summing expression is still sitting in the live database.

The one part of the claim I would restate: "the code is random" is true but is not the real problem — Math.random codes would be fine if anything checked them. The real problem is that nothing checks them, so the code is decorative.

findings.title: A day-pass never leaves status 'active' — nothing expires or redeems it
findings.evidence: buyDayPass inserts status:'active' (api.ts:809) and no code path ever updates it. Live: select count(*) filter (where status='active') = 6, filter (where status='active' and expires_at < now()) = 6, expired = 0, used = 0. Catalog check: zero non-internal triggers on public.day_passes; pg_cron is not installed (relation cron.job does not exist; pg_extension = plpgsql, pg_stat_statements, uuid-ossp, pgcrypto, supabase_vault, postgis); the only function referencing day_passes is admin_dashboard, which only reads. The 'expired' value exists in the CHECK constraint (schema4_admin.sql:157) and in web/admin/src/lib/types.ts:150 but is unreachable.
findings.failure: Pass 29AL0H at iron-bay was created 2026-08-31 10:35:15 with expires_at 2026-08-31 19:59:59Z. Today (2026-09-08) the row still reads status='active'. Any surface that trusts the status column — the admin 'Aktiv day-pass · canlı' tile, the gym owner count filtered .in(['active','used']) — describes an 8-day-dead pass as current.
findings.fix: Stop storing a status the app never maintains. Either derive it (a view / generated expression comparing expires_at to now(), so 'expired' is a fact rather than a write nobody performs), or add a server-side stamping RPC plus a scheduled job, and have every read filter on expires_at > now() until that exists.

findings.title: The door code exists only in React state — the member loses it the moment they leave the screen
findings.evidence: const [dayPass, setDayPass] = useState<{code,expiresAt}|null>(null) is plain component state; nothing writes it to the zustand store or to disk (no dayPass reference anywhere under src/store). The only client reads of the table are getGymDayPasses (src/lib/roles.ts:358, owner-side count), so there is no query that ever fetches the signed-in member's own passes. There is no 'my passes' route in src/app.
findings.failure: A member on the gym page taps the pass, sees code JV8EBC and the instruction «Resepsiyada bu kodu göstər — bu gün 23:59-a qədər keçərlidir» ([id].tsx:410-413), then backs out to walk to the gym. On return the card is gone, the button has reset from 'Day-pass aktivdir' to '1 günlük · 6 ₼', and the only copy of the code they were told to show at reception is unrecoverable — while the row sits in the database.
findings.fix: Read the member's own passes back from the server (dp_user_read already permits it: auth.uid() = user_id) on screen mount, and render any unexpired pass instead of relying on the local state left over from the insert.

findings.title: Nothing at reception can look a code up, and RLS gives the gym no way to redeem one
findings.evidence: The gym owner panel's entire day-pass surface is <Row label="Qeydə alınan day-pass" value={count} /> (gym/index.tsx:318), fed by getGymDayPasses which does .select('id').eq('gym_id',gymId).in('status',['active','used']) (src/lib/roles.ts:358-361) — codes are never selected. grep for ".eq('code'", 'redeem', 'markUsed', 'mark_used' across src, web/admin and supabase returns nothing. Live policies on day_passes: dp_owner_read is SELECT-only (owns_gym(gym_id)); the sole UPDATE policy is dp_admin_update = admin_at_least(auth.uid(),'ops'). src/app/gym/claim.tsx:208 nevertheless promises the owner panel shows «zal kodu və day-pass».
findings.failure: A member walks in and reads out JV8EBC. The owner opens their panel and sees the number 6 and the sentence 'SPOT ödəniş qəbul etmir'. There is no field to type the code into, no list to match it against, and no control to mark it used — so reception has to either turn the person away or let anyone who says any six characters in.
findings.fix: Give the owner a lookup: an owner-scoped RPC that takes (gym_id, code) and returns a single verdict (valid / already used / expired / unknown), plus an owner UPDATE path that stamps status='used'. Both must be server-side; a client that reads the whole pass list would leak every code for that gym.

findings.title: admin_dashboard() throws on every call — it still sums the dropped commission column
findings.evidence: Executed live: select public.admin_dashboard(); → ERROR: 42703: column "commission" does not exist, CONTEXT: SQL function "admin_dashboard" during startup. pg_get_functiondef shows the live body still contains 'revenue_commission', (select coalesce(sum(commission),0) from public.day_passes where status in ('used','active')). schema27_trust_columns.sql:194 dropped the column but never recreated the function; the live column list for day_passes is code, expires_at, gym_id, id, price, purchased_at, refund_reason, refunded_at, status, user_id — no commission. The error is planned, not conditional: it fires even for a non-admin caller because the whole CASE expression must be planned.
findings.failure: An admin opens the panel. supabase.rpc('admin_dashboard') at web/admin/src/screens/Dashboard.tsx:36 and App.tsx:35 destructure only { data } and never inspect .error, so data is null: all five KPI tiles render '—' and every sidebar badge silently disappears, with no message saying the query failed. Separately, a revenue-summing expression is still live in the production database, against the absolute no-money rule.
findings.fix: Recreate admin_dashboard without the revenue_commission key at all (not merely without the sum), and make both call sites surface .error instead of silently degrading to '—'.

findings.title: One person can create unlimited passes for the same gym on the same day
findings.evidence: dp_user_insert on public.day_passes for insert with check (auth.uid() = user_id) is the only gate — no rate limit, no per-day predicate. Live index list for day_passes is exactly day_passes_pkey and day_passes_status_idx (status, purchased_at DESC): no unique index on code, none on (user_id, gym_id, date). Live data shows iron-bay issued two passes on 2026-08-31 one second apart (29AL0H at 10:35:15, BN6UN7 at 10:35:16). The only thing that ever stops a second tap is the client-local disabled={buyingPass || !!dayPass} at src/app/(tabs)/discover/gym/[id].tsx:392, which resets whenever the screen unmounts.
findings.failure: Because the code is also lost on unmount (see the useState finding), the natural user behaviour — reopen the gym page because the code vanished — creates a fresh row every time. Ten reopens produce ten 'active' passes for one person at one gym on one day, and the gym owner's «Qeydə alınan day-pass» count reports ten visitors that never happened.
findings.fix: Add a partial unique index on (user_id, gym_id, (purchased_at at time zone 'Asia/Baku')::date) so a second pass for the same day is refused by the database, and have the client treat that refusal as 'you already have a pass' by showing the existing one.

findings.title: «Aktiv day-pass · canlı» is a fabricated live number
findings.evidence: { label: 'Aktiv day-pass', val: String(k.daypass_active), dark: true, sub: 'canlı' } is fed by 'daypass_active', (select count(*) from public.day_passes where status='active') (schema4_admin.sql:307). Nothing ever moves a row off 'active' (proven above), and expires_at is not consulted. Live: all 6 rows are 'active', all 6 expired on 2026-08-31 or 2026-09-01.
findings.failure: Once the commission crash is fixed, this tile will print 'Aktiv day-pass 6 · canlı' on 2026-09-08 when the newest of those passes died seven days earlier. The word 'canlı' (live) asserts a present-tense fact the query never measured.
findings.fix: Count where expires_at > now() and status = 'active', or drop the tile until expiry is real. A count that ignores expiry must not be labelled 'canlı'.

findings.title: The validity window is written by the phone and enforced by nobody
findings.evidence: const end = new Date(); end.setHours(23,59,59,0) uses the device's own clock and timezone, and expires_at is then inserted by the client (api.ts:810). The authenticated INSERT grant covers expires_at (column privileges: code, expires_at, gym_id, id, price, purchased_at, refund_reason, refunded_at, status, user_id) and dp_user_insert checks only auth.uid() = user_id, so the server accepts whatever timestamp arrives. There is no server-side default or CHECK bounding expires_at.
findings.failure: A member whose phone is on UTC (travelling, or an emulator) gets a pass the card advertises as valid «bu gün 23:59-a qədər» but stored as 03:59 Baku the following morning; a member whose phone clock is a day ahead gets one dated tomorrow. And since the value is client-supplied, a modified client can write expires_at a year out. The screen's promise at [id].tsx:412 is enforced by nothing on the server.
findings.fix: Let the database own the window: default expires_at to date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'Asia/Baku') + interval '1 day' - interval '1 second', and revoke the client's ability to insert the column.

findings.title: Codes are non-cryptographic, not unique, and can be shorter than six characters
findings.evidence: const code = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8).toUpperCase(). Math.random is not a CSPRNG and its output stream is predictable from prior draws. slice(2,8) assumes the base-36 expansion always has at least six fractional digits — for a value with a short expansion it yields fewer (0.5 → '0.i' → 'I'). No unique index on day_passes.code exists in the live catalog, and no insert ever checks for a collision.
findings.failure: Today this is inert because nothing validates a code. The moment the reception lookup in the finding above is built, two members can hold the same six characters at the same gym and the lookup has no way to tell them apart, and a short code narrows the space to a handful of values.
findings.fix: Generate the code in the database (e.g. from gen_random_bytes via pgcrypto) with a fixed length and a unique index on code, and retry on conflict — never let the client choose its own credential.

findings.title: A deleted account's passes survive as ownerless rows and are still counted for the gym
findings.evidence: day_passes_user_id_fkey is FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, and neither schema40_delete_account.sql nor schema52_delete_own_content.sql mentions day_passes (grep returns nothing). getGymDayPasses filters only on gym_id and status, never on user_id. Live: all 6 rows have user_id = null while their gym_id and price still point at real gyms (iron-bay 5.00, volt-gym 7.00, atlas-fit 6.00, peak-house 4.00 — matching the gyms' own day_pass prices).
findings.failure: After a member deletes their account, the pass row stays and keeps feeding the owner panel's «Qeydə alınan day-pass» figure, so the count includes visits by people who no longer exist and whose row can never be attributed, refunded, or explained.
findings.fix: Decide explicitly: either delete the member's day_passes in the account-deletion path alongside their other content, or exclude user_id is null from the owner count and say in the panel what the number covers.

explanation:
Verified each part of the claim against the live DB (project oezzgcumwprpoqekmlop) and the client source.

**1. `public.chats` — RLS on, ZERO policies: the FACT is true, the IMPLIED HOLE is REFUTED.**
`pg_class` for public.chats: `relrowsecurity = true`, `n_policies = 0` (confirmed via pg_policies). But it is CLOSED, not open, and doubly so:
- `information_schema.role_table_grants` for public.chats returns ONE row: `service_role`. There is no grant to `anon` or `authenticated` at all.
- Empirical proof — `begin; set local role anon; select count(*) from public.chats; rollback;` returns:
  `ERROR: 42501: permission denied for table chats`
- `select count(*) from public.chats` = **0 rows**.
This is deliberate and documented: `D:\spot\supabase\schema25_lock_chats.sql` deletes the four fabricated conversations, drops both policies, keeps RLS on, and does `revoke all on public.chats from anon, authenticated`. The table comment reads "CLOSED to all clients (schema25)". So `chats` is genuinely dead weight (empty table, no client reader, no owner/participant column), but it is quarantined correctly — a table with RLS on and no policies denies everything, and the missing GRANT denies it a second time. No security finding.

**2. `meals` — REFUTED, still live.**
`meals` has 1 policy (`meals_read`, SELECT, `qual = true`, role public) and **4 rows**. `useMeals()` at `D:\spot\src\lib\hooks.ts:390` is imported and called by three live screens: `D:\spot\src\app\(tabs)\workout\nutrition\index.tsx:15,156`, `D:\spot\src\app\(tabs)\workout\nutrition\meal\[id].tsx:14,22`, and `D:\spot\src\app\(tabs)\workout\nutrition\shopping.tsx:11,49`. Not dead.

**3. `shop_items` — CONFIRMED dead.**
1 policy (`shop_items_read`, SELECT true, public), **7 rows** seeded at `D:\spot\supabase\schema2.sql:255-258` with invented grocery prices. `useShopItems()` at `D:\spot\src\lib\hooks.ts:396` is exported and **never imported anywhere** — grep for `useShopItems` across `src` and `web` returns only its own definition. `shopping.tsx` builds the list from meal ingredients via `buildList(meals)` instead. Nothing in the app or the admin SPA touches `shop_items`.

**4. `profiles.visibility` — CONFIRMED written-never-read, and it has a live user-facing consequence.**
Nothing in the database consults it. I scanned every angle and all came back empty:
- pg_policies where `qual||with_check ILIKE '%visibility%'` → 0 rows. The real gate, `profiles_read`, is `((user_id = auth.uid()) OR is_admin(auth.uid()) OR (COALESCE(show_in_gym_list, true) AND NOT blocked_between(id, my_profile_id())) OR has_relationship_with(id))` — it uses `show_in_gym_list`, never `visibility`.
- `information_schema.views` with `visibility` in the definition → 0 rows.
- Non-internal trigger functions whose `prosrc` mentions `visibility` → 0 rows.
- All `public` PL functions whose `prosrc` mentions visibility / day_cells / days_left / leaderboard / chats → **0 rows**.
Client side it is only written and echoed: written at `D:\spot\src\app\(tabs)\profile\privacy.tsx:35` and `D:\spot\src\store\appStore.ts:328`, read back into state at `appStore.ts:260`, listed in the select at `D:\spot\src\lib\api.ts:32` and `D:\spot\web\admin\src\screens\Users.tsx:123` (fetched, never rendered). No send/message path branches on it — grep for `match-only` finds only the store default and the two toggle sites.
The profile settings screen already recognised this and removed its toggle, with the reason in the code (`profile/privacy.tsx:205-210`): "It wrote `profiles.visibility` and NOTHING read it back … A control that promises protection it does not perform is worse than no control." **The identical toggle is still shipping on onboarding step 6** — see finding 1.

**5. `challenges.progress / leaderboard / day_cells / days_left` — CONFIRMED dead as displayed data.**
DB state (3 challenge rows): `progress <> 0` on 3 rows, `days_left not null` on 3 rows, `day_cells` non-empty on 1 row, `leaderboard` non-empty on **0** rows.
`mapChallenge` at `D:\spot\src\lib\hooks.ts:112-113` still pulls three of them into the `Challenge` object (`progress: r.progress ?? 0`, `daysLeft: r.days_left`, `leaderboard: (r.leaderboard ?? [])`); `day_cells` is not mapped at all. No screen renders any of them — grep for `daysLeft` / `leaderboard` / `c.progress` across `src/app` returns zero render sites. Both challenge screens deliberately compute from real local logs: `D:\spot\src\app\challenge\index.tsx:40` (`useLast7Days()` from the user's own workouts/check-ins) and `D:\spot\src\app\challenge\[id].tsx:26-27` ("the seed `c.progress` is never shown"), plus explicit honest copy at `[id].tsx:78-79` ("No countdown … a static seed number rendered as 'Qalıb: 11 gün' would be a fabricated live count") and `[id].tsx:105` ("Uydurma sıralama göstərmirik"). So the columns are genuinely dead — the honesty work is intact — but the mapper still carries the seed numbers into the shared type.

**Bonus, provable from the grant query:** `meals` and `shop_items` grant `anon` and `authenticated` `DELETE, INSERT, UPDATE, TRUNCATE` while carrying only a SELECT policy. RLS denies the DML today (no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy = denied), and PostgREST cannot issue TRUNCATE, so this is not reachable now — but TRUNCATE is not RLS-checked and the write block rests entirely on "no policy exists". Contrast `chats`, which was properly stripped with `revoke all`.

findings.title: Onboarding step 6 ships a privacy toggle that enforces nothing — the exact control the settings screen removed as dishonest
findings.evidence: onboarding/privacy.tsx:36-41 renders <ToggleRow title="Yalnız match olanlar yaza bilər" sub="Sən qəbul etməyincə heç kim birbaşa mesaj yaza bilməz. Zal üzvünə isə bir dəfə 'sual' formatı ilə yazmaq olar." value={visibility === 'match-only'} onValueChange={(v) => setPrivacy({ visibility: v ? 'match-only' : 'everyone' })} />. That writes profiles.visibility (appStore.ts:328 -> updateMyProfile) and NOTHING reads it: pg_policies with 'visibility' in qual/with_check = 0 rows; public PL functions mentioning visibility = 0 rows; views = 0 rows; trigger functions = 0 rows. The actual profiles_read policy gates on show_in_gym_list, not visibility. The messaging policies (messages_send) gate on in_thread(thread_id) / thread_blocked, never on visibility. The screen is reachable — src/app/onboarding/profile.tsx:74 does router.push('/onboarding/privacy'). The settings copy of this same toggle was already deleted for this reason, with the reason written into the code at src/app/(tabs)/profile/privacy.tsx:205-210: «It wrote `profiles.visibility` and NOTHING read it back — neither position changed who could message you — and the footer advertised a one-off 'sual' channel that does not exist in the app. A control that promises protection it does not perform is worse than no control … Put the toggle back only when a send path actually reads `visibility`.»
findings.failure: A new user reaching onboarding step 6 sees «Yalnız match olanlar yaza bilər» switched on and is told «Sən qəbul etməyincə heç kim birbaşa mesaj yaza bilməz». They leave it on, believing direct messages are blocked until they accept. The value is persisted to profiles.visibility='match-only' (1 of 1 profile rows in the live DB currently holds exactly that value), and no policy, function, trigger, view or client send path ever consults it — so message permission is identical whether the switch is on or off. The subtitle additionally advertises a one-off «sual» channel to gym members that does not exist anywhere in the app. This is a privacy promise the product does not keep, stated in the user's own language, on a screen they cannot skip.
findings.fix: Delete the first ToggleRow from src/app/onboarding/privacy.tsx (lines 36-41) and replace it with the same honest statement the settings screen now shows — the rule that IS enforced (a chat opens only after both sides accept a match request) — as static copy, not a switch. Keep the second ToggleRow: show_in_gym_list is genuinely enforced by the profiles_read policy. Restore the toggle only once a send path actually reads visibility.

findings.title: shop_items is a dead table: its only reader, useShopItems, is exported but never imported
findings.evidence: `export const useShopItems = () => useList<ShopItem>(mockShop, async () => { const { data } = await supabase.from('shop_items').select('*').order('ord'); ... })` at src/lib/hooks.ts:396-400. grep for `useShopItems` across src/ and web/ returns only this definition — no importer. The shopping screen builds its list from meal ingredients instead: src/app/(tabs)/workout/nutrition/shopping.tsx:49 `const meals = useMeals();` then `buildList(meals)`, documented at shopping.tsx:24-25 («The list is built from the ingredients of the meals in the plan — so "qida planından yaradıldı" is literally true»). Live DB: shop_items has 7 rows, seeded at supabase/schema2.sql:255-258 with invented prices (8, 12, 3, 4, 2.5, 6, 35), and one policy `shop_items_read` SELECT using (true) to public.
findings.failure: Nothing is broken on screen today — the table is invisible. The hazard is the same shape as the one schema25 had to clean up for `chats`: a world-readable table of seeded rows carrying made-up numbers sitting one import away from a screen. The moment anyone wires `useShopItems()` into the shopping screen, the app renders seven invented grocery prices as if they were real, and useList's mock-fallback (`mockShop`) means an empty or failed fetch silently shows src/data/nutrition.ts's hardcoded list instead of an empty state.
findings.fix: Delete useShopItems from src/lib/hooks.ts (and the now-unused `shoppingList as mockShop` / `ShopItem` imports at hooks.ts:12), then close the table the way schema25 closed chats: delete the seed rows, drop shop_items_read, keep RLS on, and revoke all on public.shop_items from anon, authenticated.

findings.title: mapChallenge still carries seed progress/days_left/leaderboard into the Challenge object no screen may render
findings.evidence: src/lib/hooks.ts:112-113: `progress: r.progress ?? 0, target: r.target, unit: r.unit, daysLeft: r.days_left, reward: r.reward, participants: r.participants ?? 0, leaderboard: (r.leaderboard ?? []) as LeaderRow[]`. Live DB challenges (3 rows): progress non-zero on 3 rows, days_left not null on 3 rows, day_cells non-empty on 1 row, leaderboard non-empty on 0 rows. day_cells is not mapped at all — no reference to `day_cells` or `dayCells` from the DB anywhere in src (challenge/index.tsx:40 computes dayCells locally via useLast7Days() from the device's real workouts and check-ins). The two challenge screens deliberately ignore the mapped seed values: challenge/[id].tsx:26-27 «Real progress from the user's own logs — the seed `c.progress` is never shown», [id].tsx:78-79 «No countdown: … a static seed number rendered as "Qalıb: 11 gün" would be a fabricated live count», [id].tsx:105 «Reytinq cədvəli iştirakçı datası toplananda açılacaq. Uydurma sıralama göstərmirik.»
findings.failure: Correct on screen today, but the Challenge type still exposes `progress: 8`, `daysLeft: 11` and a `leaderboard` array sourced from seed rows, with nothing in the type or the mapper marking them as not-measured. Any future `{c.daysLeft} gün qalıb` or `{c.progress}` — the natural thing to write given the field exists and is populated — prints a static seed number as a live measurement, which is precisely the fabrication three separate code comments were written to prevent.
findings.fix: Stop mapping them: drop `progress`, `daysLeft` and `leaderboard` from mapChallenge (hooks.ts:112-113) and from the Challenge interface in src/data/challenges.ts, so the seed values cannot be reached from a component at all. Callers already compute the real numbers via useChallengeProgress() and useLast7Days(). Then drop the four columns (progress, days_left, leaderboard, day_cells) from public.challenges.

findings.title: anon and authenticated hold INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on meals and shop_items; only the absence of a policy blocks writes
findings.evidence: information_schema.role_table_grants for public.meals and public.shop_items each return anon = DELETE,INSERT,REFERENCES,SELECT,TRIGGER,TRUNCATE,UPDATE and authenticated = the same set. pg_policies shows exactly one policy per table — meals_read / shop_items_read, SELECT, qual=true, role public — created by the loop at supabase/schema2.sql:156-160. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy exists, so RLS denies those today. Contrast public.chats, which schema25_lock_chats.sql stripped properly with `revoke all on public.chats from anon, authenticated` — its grant listing shows service_role only, and `set local role anon; select count(*) from public.chats` fails with «42501: permission denied for table chats» rather than merely returning zero rows.
findings.failure: Not reachable through PostgREST as it stands: an anon DELETE on meals is refused by RLS, and PostgREST exposes no TRUNCATE verb. The defect is that the write block is a single point of failure — TRUNCATE is not subject to row-level security at all, and one permissive policy added later, or one `alter table … disable row level security` during a migration, instantly makes both tables world-writable to anyone holding the publishable key shipped in the APK. That is the exact posture schema25's header describes as how the fabricated inbox shipped the first time.
findings.fix: Mirror schema25: revoke all on public.meals, public.shop_items from anon, authenticated; then grant select (only) back to anon, authenticated. Note the project's own trap here — the table-level GRANT must be revoked before a narrower grant is issued, or the broad one keeps winning.
